claim: Two admissible increasing reciprocal-divergent envelopes need not have an admissible common majorant; their sum and maximum can have reciprocal-convergent integrals.
remaining_gap: This is a counterexample to an envelope inference, not to (H)-stability or even to closure of the existential Rao class.

remaining_gap: The unrestricted hypothesis does not imply the domination or density assumptions; special case is already in Hu-Sun 2018.

claim: Finite energy for a sum need not imply finite energy for either summand, even when the two summands and the sum all satisfy (H) and have transition densities.
remaining_gap: This disproves a proposed energy-transfer lemma, not the original question: the constructed sum satisfies (H).

claim: Resolvent densities of independent Levy summands do not alone imply resolvent densities of their sum.
remaining_gap: The deterministic summands fail (H), so the claim does not establish a density obstruction under the original (H) premises.
checks: Direct resolvent computation for deterministic motions t and -t; sum resolvent is a point mass.

claim: For every pair of independent R^n-valued Levy processes satisfying (H), their sum satisfies (H).

claim: Under a common admissible EKFR-type decomposition for two independent Levy exponents, the sum satisfies (H) if it has resolvent densities and its excessive-cancellation frequency set has integrable reciprocal sum denominator.
remaining_gap: The common decomposition, sum density, and exceptional-set integral are not consequences of arbitrary (H)+(H); individual densities are unnecessary when (H) is already supplied.

claim: In particular, two common-envelope EKFR processes with same-sign imaginary exponents almost everywhere have an (H) independent sum, assuming resolvent densities.
remaining_gap: Does not treat unrelated envelopes, unrestricted cancellation, or all (H) processes.

remaining_gap: The functions are not Levy exponents; this is not a counterexample to E0027 or to closure for actual EKFR Levy processes.
